title: The trombone job at the Blue Rhythm Club and trumpeter Arnold Metoyer
summary: Desvigne and Manetta recall a dance where the crowd wanted him on trumpet not trombone, and praise trumpeter Arnold Metoyer, who later led the Desvigne Orchestra.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: That's the only one for sure. That's right. Well, there's that one other dance too, that Vest, or somebody told me once where you started to play trombone, and the people that had hired the band, they didn't know what was going on when they saw you on trombone. They thought something's wrong here.
Well, they just thought I couldn't play the trombone, and they wanted me to play the trumpet, you see.

That's the blue rhythm club, we'll see. Blue rhythm club. Blue rhythm club. It's a big open place. All that in those trombone, so... Yeah, big guy in the dance field. Well, I know, but I don't see... It's my own band. It's my own band.

I understand that. They're playing for them people, but play this trumpet. The thing is, I had a trumpet player, I probably didn't play more trumpet than I could play, but still they wanted me to play the trumpet, you see what I mean?
You know you had that that night? You know you had? No, I don't.
I know all in Lillistat. You sure know. And you was playing the trombone?

What did? I know I'm a twi-a, and Louis Armstrong. So when they walk in, the fella said, he said, what do you say? Now you pull a little over my eyes, uh-uh, uh-uh, uh-uh. I don't know what I say. You remember he had to put a trombone down? And he take the horn up, and I know, this nigga out here fool with the music, you know? He was satisfied. Yeah, he was beatin' by it. He was satisfied. He was satisfied so long he saw us playin' the place, he started packin' up, you know? Well, he was satisfied he saw us stayin' there with that horn, that trumpet.

And Arnold was a fine trumpet player. He played all right here. Juarez, Tijuana, he played all around Mexico, you know? Because I remember when I first met Arnold Matoir, and he used to tell me about Tijuana and Juarez while we was playin' there. But he used to do very nice trumpet. Oh, he was? Yeah. Yeah. Nice trumpet play.
I never got to know him or hear him or know anything about him, very little except what some people have told me.
He played just like those Mexican guys, you know? Yeah. Yeah.

Yeah, and then when he got on the boats, then they put the old trombone down and went back on his trumpet. Then, uh, made a trip, then you come outta town, you organize your band, the Deadly Orchestra. Right? Yes, right. That's right. Used to be.
